svg.aria-label: Relative estimators: the additive offset model, how anchoring cancels the receptor offset, the experiments that tested it, identifiability, the selectivity bootstrap and the single-mutation head.
svg.text: The scorer's error is a receptor offset + a peptide offset + noise
S(P, R) = ΔG(P, R) + b(R) + c(P) + η
ΔG(P, R): the true binding free energy, which we want. η: noise.
b(R) is large and cannot be predicted from structure; it is shared by every peptide on one receptor.
Anchoring: measured peptides on the same receptor cancel b(R)
ΔG_pred(P, R) = Σ_k w_k · [ ΔG_exp(ref_k) + S(P, R) − S(ref_k, R) ]
b(R) appears in both scores, so it cancels
so ΔG_pred ≈ ΔG(P, R) + Σ w_k [c(P) − c(ref_k)] + noise
needs measured Kd values on the same receptor (identity ≥ 0.90); otherwise the plain score is returned
Predicting a held-out cell of the matrix
spread of b(R): 2.18 of c(P): 2.43 kcal/mol
control: anchors from the wrong receptor give r = 0.12
Matrix factorization with both offsets barely beats the simple anchor, and the offset cannot be predicted from structure (best similarity correlation +0.084).
Why only differences of offsets are identifiable
adding the same constant to every b and subtracting it
from every c leaves all four scores unchanged
so b(R1) − b(R2) is knowable, but b(R1) alone is not
Selectivity ΔΔG = ΔG_T − ΔG_O with a bootstrap interval
pass only if the whole 95% interval lies on the right side of zero
ΔG is the MM-GBSA score when it ran, otherwise the Vina score; the entropy-corrected hybrid is excluded
illustration with made-up scores; the procedure is the real one
Single-residue changes need their own head
OppA K-X-K series: 19 tripeptides, one varying position, 3.00 kcal/mol span
the median feature moves only 14% of its standard deviation per substitution
SKEMPI v2: 4,956 single mutations in 319 complexes, MAE 1.062 kcal/mol
OppA result is suggestive, not significant (n = 18)
